title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten University of Michigan Library study environments with documented locations, seating, features, and access considerations.

cards.title: Asia Library Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library North, Floor 4, Room 421
cards.notes: Use the desks, booths, or open tables for quiet work; expect occasional activity when classes or events use adjoining rooms.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, light-filled room combining desks, booths, tables, and the Oka Tadoku Room.
cards.evidence_claim: The room has study desks, booths, open tables, natural light, and a quiet noise level.
cards.source_title: Asia Library Reading Room | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Hatcher North on floor 4; occasional class or event noise is documented.

cards.title: Hatcher North Stacks Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library North, multiple stack floors
cards.notes: Follow the stack-floor directions to the south-end tables; choose a floor with the seating style that fits your solo or quiet group work.
cards.short_summary: Quiet tables and carrel-style desks distributed across seven stack floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Study seating is available on seven Hatcher North stack floors, near south-end windows, with tables and individual desks varying by floor.
cards.source_title: Hatcher North Stacks Study Tables | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Use the floor-specific stack entrances and directional markings described by the library.

cards.title: Hatcher South Open Carrels
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library South, Floors 4 and 5
cards.notes: Settle into an unreserved, windowed carrel for reading or writing; bring headphones if nearby sound would interrupt focused work.
cards.short_summary: Individual desk-and-window cubicles around the Hatcher South stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: These quiet carrels provide a small desk, chair, and window on floors 4 and 5; they are open and not soundproof.
cards.source_title: Hatcher South Open Carrels | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Open carrels are on floors 4 and 5; floor-3 carrels are separately bookable.

cards.title: Hatcher Floor 6
cards.subtitle: Hatcher Library South, Floor 6
cards.notes: Choose the open seating area for armchairs or divided tables, and use the Special Collections area only during its separate availability window.
cards.short_summary: Quiet sixth-floor seating with campus views, armchairs, tables, and privacy dividers.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 6 has quiet study seating with views of the Law Quad and Michigan Stadium; the SCRC study space is available weekdays until 5pm.
cards.source_title: Hatcher Floor 6 | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: The Special Collections Research Center portion is available Monday–Friday until 5pm; other seating follows building access.

cards.title: Shapiro Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Shapiro Library, Floor 3, Room 3100
cards.notes: Take a long table for individual focus, or select a smaller table or armchair along the exterior walls for a different posture.
cards.short_summary: A quiet third-floor reading room with padded chairs, lamps, and natural light.
cards.evidence_claim: The quiet room has long tables with padded chairs and lamps, plus smaller tables and armchairs near large windows.
cards.source_title: Shapiro Reading Room | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Located at the south end of Clark Commons on Shapiro Library’s third floor.

cards.title: Clark Commons Computing Spaces
cards.subtitle: Shapiro Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Bring a laptop for the extended displays, or use a shared screen and nearby whiteboards when a project needs collaborative setup.
cards.short_summary: Conversational computing seating with external monitors, shared screens, and printing nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Clark Commons offers extended-monitor bays, shared screens, a computing site with printing, whiteboards, and accessible seating.
cards.source_title: Clark Commons Computing Spaces | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: This is a conversational third-floor Shapiro Library space; it includes computing and printing areas.

cards.entity_name: Taubman Health Sciences Library Study Space
cards.title: Taubman Health Sciences Library Study Space
cards.subtitle: Taubman Health Sciences Library, Floor 4
cards.notes: Use adjustable desks, pod chairs, booths, or table seating for focused work; reserve collaboration needs for the display-equipped west-wall areas.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, light-filled library space with varied seating, computing, and collaboration displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The fourth-floor space offers adjustable desks, pod chairs, booths, tables, external monitors, and three collaboration areas.
cards.source_title: Taubman Health Sciences Library Study Space | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Extended hours require MCard entry and are limited to specified medical and graduate student populations.

cards.entity_name: Art, Architecture, and Engineering Library Floor 2 Stacks Spaces
cards.title: AAEL Floor 2 Stacks Spaces
cards.subtitle: Art, Architecture, and Engineering Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Head through the northeast double doors from the lobby, then choose window counters, individual desks, large tables, or corner armchairs.
cards.short_summary: Quiet second-floor stacks seating inside the Duderstadt Center with several work surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The quiet stacks area includes bar-height window counters, individual desks, large tables, corner armchairs, natural light, and wheelchair access.
cards.source_title: Art, Architecture, and Engineering Library Floor 2 Stacks Spaces | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Enter the Duderstadt Center’s floor 2, then pass from lobby spaces through the northeast double doors.

cards.title: Fine Arts Library Floor 2
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Library, Tappan Hall, Floor 2
cards.notes: Enter through Tappan Hall’s second-floor doors and choose a large wood table or a deeper-in-the-stacks table; keep food wrapped and drinks covered.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, high-ceilinged, book-lined room with large wood tables and window light.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor has quiet study space with large wooden tables, book stacks, natural light, and restrictions to covered drinks and wrapped food.
cards.source_title: Fine Arts Library Floor 2 | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Enter via Tappan Hall’s second floor; only covered drinks and wrapped food are permitted.

cards.title: Music Library Floors 3 and 4
cards.subtitle: Music Library, Floors 3 and 4
cards.notes: Use floor 3 for window tables or armchair clusters, and plan for stairs to floor 4 unless staff can assist with the elevator.
cards.short_summary: Quiet, airy North Campus study floors with tables, armchairs, and wooded views.
cards.evidence_claim: All Music Library study space is on floors 3 and 4, with natural light, tables, armchairs, and wheelchair accessibility.
cards.source_title: Music Library Floors 3 and 4 | University of Michigan Library
cards.access_notes: Floor-4 primary access is by stairs; request staff help at the Information Services Desk for elevator use. Covered drinks and small snacks only.
